title: Per-route tiered batching automation with safe commit/rollback checkpoints
creator: Amina Patel
description: Implement an automated per-route and per-customer policy engine that recommends and applies batching/caching profiles by tier with guarded commit checkpoints. The feature should: 1) segment traffic by route signature and customer tier; 2) compute per-segment batching and KV-cache suggestions from historical latency, token distribution, and cost telemetry; 3) support allowlists and denylists at route and customer level; 4) expose a dry-run simulator that predicts cost/latency delta and runs in sandbox mode; 5) perform staged canary applies with automatic rollback on safety signals; 6) integrate with Console rollouts so PMs/operators can approve or abort. This ticket contains the runtime hooks, orchestration logic for safe commits (snapshot + checkpoint), and the monitoring triggers for auto-rollback. The implementation must be able to: a) accept suggestions from Optimize heuristics, b) persist a checkpoint before any live change, c) route a configurable percentage of traffic to the updated profile, d) evaluate SLA/cost signals and revert to checkpoint if thresholds are violated.
acceptance_criteria: Policy engine accepts segmentation rules based on route signature, customer tier label, and explicit allowlist/denylist entries
Batch/caching suggestion API returns profile with expected token-cost delta and 90/95/99p latency estimates
Dry-run simulator ingests 7-day traffic and produces a cost/latency forecast within ±15% of actual when applied to a sandbox cluster
Apply pipeline creates a checkpoint snapshot, performs a canary apply (configurable traffic fraction), and auto-rolls back if any of the safety signals fire
Safety signals include: error rate increase > 0.5pp over baseline, 95p latency regression > 20%, token-per-request cost increase > 10% without throughput improvement
Console rollout UI shows policy diff, predicted cost impact, canary fraction, and a manual approve/abort control
Operator-facing runbook updated with explicit rollback steps and a one-click rollback from Console
End-to-end e2e tests cover dry-run -> canary -> full rollout -> rollback flow in CI
Telemetry emits tags for applied policy id, checkpoint id, canary_fraction, and rollback_reason
tasks: Design: finalize segmentation schema and priority precedence (explicit allowlist > tenant tier > route defaults)
Runtime: add policy hook to routing layer to consult per-route profile cache
Orchestration: implement checkpoint creation and metadata store for config snapshots
Simulator: build dry-run cost/latency estimator using sampled 7-day traces
Rollout engine: implement canary traffic splitter and evaluators for safety signals
Console: add rollout UX for previewing predicted impact and approving canaries
Telemetry: add rollout and safety signal metrics to the observability pipeline
Tests: unit tests for policy precedence and integration tests for canary + rollback
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting with Prod, Runtime, and Optimize teams. Agreed segmentation keys: route_name, route_version, customer_tier, and customer_id allowlist. Decision: allowlist entries take precedence over denylist for emergency overrides.

2026-03-04: PoC of dry-run simulator completed against synthetic trace. Initial cost estimates optimistic — observed median underprediction for long-tail seq lengths. Action: include sequence-length bucketing in estimator.
2026-03-06: Runtime patched to surface per-route profile hook. Hook returns candidate profile but not yet applied. Integration test added. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4825

2026-03-08: Design review with Security and Console teams. Security requested audit log entries for checkpoints and emphasized KMS usage for any persisted checkpoint metadata (we will not store secret material).

2026-03-10: Canary engine prototype ready in dev cluster. Ran two internal canaries against low-volume routes; one canary triggered rollback due to 95p latency regression. Behavior validated end-to-end. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/214

2026-03-12: Blocker: metrics pipeline lag (current 3m ingest latency) makes rollback slow for short-lived regressions. Mitigation: add a fast-path aggregate stream for canary signals; estimate 2 sprint work to fully fix. Temporary plan: increase canary window to 10 minutes for now.
